ranking_note: Authored from the before descriptions at commit 1e8ff6f8bbc232b84b12f6888a85dafc502d5f8b, frozen before the rewrite; protocol per /playbooks:skill-authoring ## Measurement. Competitors are the context-budget setup skill (user-invoked, a near-miss target) and the nearby model-invoked skills.

queries.request: Before I type anything, how many tokens does Claude Code already load into a fresh session?
My context seems half full the moment I open a new chat. Can you break down where that comes from?
Which of the built-in tools weigh the most in my prompt payload?
I turned off a few MCP servers yesterday. Did that actually make the startup prompt smaller?
Give me a per-item accounting of the baseline prompt size, tool by tool.
Run a measurement of the initial prompt cost, and be thorough about it, every tool.
I disabled a built-in tool in settings. Prove whether it saved anything.
Show me the ledger of every knob I've tried to shrink startup tokens and what each one gained.
Trim the single biggest contributor to my opening prompt, I'll approve it.
What does the cold-start prompt cost me per tool, measured against the real CLI?
How full is my context window right now, mid-conversation?
Why did this session use so many tokens? Walk me through it in plain words.
Which of my skills is Claude not able to see because the listing overflows?
Is node installed so the context-budget hooks can run?
What did my token spend look like across the last week of sessions?
Which hooks fired in the previous session and how slow were they?
Check whether the context-guard hook has what it needs, node and jq.
Set up context-budget for me and tell me why exact mode is unavailable.
